problem:
A man stocked a pond with $250$ fish. After $t$ weeks, the number of fish in the pond is given by the function 

$$
F(t)=250+{\int }_{0}^{t}(8x-24)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time (in weeks) since the man put the fish in the pond.

At what time is the number of fish in the pond at a minimum, and how many fish are there at that time?

choices.value: The minimum is $230$ fish after $5$ weeks
The minimum is $218$ fish after $2$ weeks
The minimum is $230$ fish after $1$ week
The minimum is $215$ fish after $4$ weeks
The minimum is $214$ fish after $3$ weeks

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Global Minimum or Maximum of a Function Given Its Rate of Change
examples.problem:
In example 2, we saw that the number of guests in a restaurant is given by

$$
T(t) = 50 + \int_0^t \left(6x^2-4\right)\,\textrm d x\,.
$$

Given that $T(t)$ has a local minimum for some $t>0,$ find the time when the number of guests is at its minimum value.
examples.worked_solution:
To find the time when the number of guests is minimized, we need to solve $\dfrac{\textrm d T}{\textrm d t} = 0.$

Differentiating $T(t)$ with respect to $t$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(50+{\int }_{0}^{t}(6{x}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(50)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(6{x}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(6{x}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}x \\  & =6{t}^{2}-4\end{aligned}
$$

Solving $\dfrac{\textrm d T}{\textrm d t} = 0$ gives

$$
6t^2-4 = 0\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}
$$

So we have $2$ critical points $t=\sqrt{\dfrac 2 3}$ and $t=0$ (the endpoint). But since the local minimum exists for $t>0,$ $t=\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$ must be the minimum value.

feedback.problem:
A zoo is tracking the number of penguins in a habitat.
They observe that new penguins arrive at a rate $r(t)$ given by the function

$$
r(t)=30{e}^{-t/2},
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in penguins per month, and $t>0$ is the time in months since the tracking began.
At the same time, $3$ penguins are transferred out each month.

If there were initially $200$ penguins in the habitat, find the expression that gives $P(t),$ the number of penguins in the habitat $t$ months after the tracking began.

$P(t)=-60{e}^{-t/2}\,+$

{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The number of penguins is increasing at a rate of $r(t)$ penguins per month and is decreasing at a rate of $3$ penguins per month. Therefore, the **rate of change** $R(t)$ of the number of penguins is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(t) & =r(t)-3 \\  & =30{e}^{-t/2}-3.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the total number $P(t)$ of penguins after $t$ months, we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(t) & =P(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}R(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =200+{\int }_{0}^{t}(30{e}^{-x/2}-3)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To ensure that our final function is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration.

We can simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(t) & =200+{\int }_{0}^{t}30{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{t}3\,\text{d}x \\  & =200+(-60{e}^{-x/2}){|}_{0}^{t}-3x{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =200+(60-60{e}^{-t/2})-3t \\  & =-60{e}^{-t/2}+260-3t\end{aligned}
$$
